_note: Illustrative multi-screen (flow) fixture for W2. Served when a request's target.kind is SCREENSHOT_SET. Three ordered screens of an email sign-up flow with cross-screen findings. Rule and heuristic ids are unverified; not real audit output. Findings follow docs/finding-schema.md; the containers are provisional. Screen convention: screen scr_<i> pairs with artifact art_<i>.

not_tested.reason: an ordered screenshot sequence shows steps but cannot prove real navigation

summary.perceived_purpose: A three-step email sign-up flow: enter email, verify a code, then a confirmation.
summary.first_impression: The steps are recognizable, but the primary button moves and step 2 gives no way back.
summary.likely_next_action: Type an email and tap Continue.
summary.headline: Recognizable flow; the primary action shifts between steps and step 2 lacks a back path.

findings.title: Primary button placement changes between step 1 and step 2
findings.flow: Sign up with email, step 1 to step 2
findings.observed: On step 1 the Continue button sits at the bottom of the screen; on step 2 the Verify button sits directly under the code field, halfway up.
findings.expected: The primary action holds a consistent position across steps so the thumb learns one target.
findings.impact: Returning to the flow, users reach for the previous position and mis-tap; consistency across steps is a core flow property.

evidence.note: Continue button at the bottom on step 1

findings.recommendation: Pin the primary action to the same position on every step of the flow.

steps: Compare the primary button's vertical position on each step of the revised flow.
retest.expected_result: The primary action is in the same position on every step.

findings.limitations: Positions estimated from static screenshots; real layout at other viewports is unknown.

findings.title: Simulated personas could not tell how to go back from step 2
findings.observed: 3 of 3 simulated personas looked for a back control on step 2 and found none; 1 said they would close the app to fix a mistyped email.
findings.expected: Personas can identify how to return to the previous step to correct the email.
findings.impact: A mistyped email on step 1 becomes a dead end; users may abandon rather than restart.

persona_signals.observation: No back arrow on step 2; unclear how to fix the email.
Would close the app and start over.

findings.recommendation: Add a visible back control to step 2 and let users edit the email without restarting.

steps: Re-run the comprehension test on step 2 of the revised flow with the same presets.
retest.expected_result: At least 2 of 3 simulated personas identify how to go back.

findings.limitations: Simulated persona behavior from static screenshots; not human participant research.

findings.title: No visible error state for an invalid email on step 1
findings.observed: The provided screens show no error or validation state for the email field; only the empty and filled states are present.
findings.expected: The flow shows how an invalid email is communicated before the user continues.
findings.impact: Missing error states are a common source of dead ends; users cannot tell why Continue does nothing.

evidence.note: Email field with no error affordance captured

findings.recommendation: Provide an inline error state for the email field and include it in the flow's screen set.

steps: Add an invalid email and capture the resulting state.
retest.expected_result: An inline, specific error message appears near the field.

findings.limitations: Absence in the provided screens is not proof the state does not exist at runtime; it was not provided for review.

findings.title: Suspected small touch target on the code inputs (step 2)
findings.observed: Each of the six code boxes samples at roughly 34 by 34 px in the screenshot's coordinate space.
findings.expected: Pointer targets are at least the platform minimum unless an exception applies.
findings.impact: Small adjacent targets are easy to mis-tap, especially one-handed; entering the code is the crux of step 2.

evidence.note: Target size estimated; rendered scale unknown

findings.recommendation: Increase the code-box size and spacing to meet the platform minimum target size.
findings.code_guidance: Set each code input to at least the platform minimum (for example 44 px on iOS) with adequate spacing.

steps: Measure the rendered size of the code inputs on a device.
retest.expected_result: Each target meets the platform minimum size or an exception applies.

automation_candidate.tool_hint: layout assertion in an e2e test

findings.limitations: Size estimated from screenshot pixels; rendered scale unknown, so reported as PARTIAL.
